title: Invocation Gateway for Micro-Adminlets — composable execution and audit shim
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Build a lightweight Invocation Gateway that wraps short-lived admin utilities (micro-adminlets) into a composable, auditable, RBAC-gated runtime so support engineers and oncall can run runbook steps as first-class tasks. The gateway will normalize inputs, attach context (request id, trace), enforce policy (RBAC, rate limits, approval checks), capture structured audit events, and route execution to sandboxed runners (k8s job, lambda, or sidecar) or a dry-run simulator.
goals: Expose a single REST/SDK endpoint for invoking micro-adminlets with typed inputs
Attach strong audit metadata to every invocation (actor, caller-route, prompt/args hash, env)
Support dry-run and simulate modes for training and playbooks
Provide pluggable safety hooks: approval gates, credential proxies, and runtime timeouts
non-goals: Do not replace large, long-running runbook orchestrators
Not intended to host stateful remediation workflows — those remain in the orchestrator
acceptance_criteria: SDK/REST endpoint documented in Console quickstart with example calls
Invocation events appear in the Console audit stream with full metadata and links to logs
RBAC policies enforced using existing identity mappings (SSO groups) — unauthorized calls return 403
Dry-run mode returns a simulated result and marks event as simulated in audit
End-to-end latency for simple adminlet <= 400ms median (excl. network) on Dedicated tier
design_notes: Architecture: lightweight gateway service accepts POST /v1/invoke with payload {adminlet: string, inputs: {...}, mode: run|dry-run, metadata: {...}}. Gateway validates input schema (JSON Schema registry), attaches context (trace_id, request_id), checks RBAC with Identity Service, optionally requires a single-step approval flow for high-risk adminlets, mounts a credential proxy token if adminlet requires elevated creds, emits pre/post invocation audit events to the telemetry pipeline, and routes to an execution backend chosen by policy (fast-path: sidecar, fallback: k8s job). Execution backends run adminlets inside constrained sandboxes with enforced resource/time limits and return structured results (status, output, artifacts_link).
tradeoffs_decisions: Decision: Use JSON Schema for adminlet input validation instead of protobufs to enable easier authoring by non-compiled tools (tradeoff: slightly slower validation).
Decision: Start with a 1-step approval flow; defer multi-party approvals to a later iteration to reduce complexity.
Tradeoff: Prefer existing identity mapping for RBAC vs building a separate role model — faster launch, less bespoke policy expressiveness.
Security: all invocation payloads are logged with their hash; actual secret material must be passed via credential proxy and never persisted in plaintext.
Fallback: if execution backend is saturated, the gateway will return 429 with suggested retry-after and a transparent fallback to queued k8s job when enabled.

safety_and_ops: Safety gates: approval-required label on adminlet manifest; kill-switch feature flag in Control Plane; runtime sandboxing via seccomp/AppArmor profiles; invocation quota per-user and per-route. Ops: add health endpoints, SLO 99.9 for gateway availability; add paginated audit API for searching invocation history and tools for replay/dry-run of historical invocations.
integration_points: Console ticket for UI quickstart: PM-4682
test_plan: Unit tests for JSON Schema validation and RBAC matrix
Integration tests exercising approval flows and dry-run mode against simulator backend
Chaos test: simulate execution backend saturation and verify 429/fallback behavior
Security review checklist and red-team validation of credential proxy boundaries
release_plan: MVP feature flag rollout to staging (runtime-2025.03-alpha), limited to Dedicated customers for 2 weeks
Collect telemetry: invocation latency, failure rate, approval wait times, audit volume
Post-mortem after 2-week pilot and expand to broader tenants with opt-in
risks: Risk: accidental logging of sensitive arguments — mitigation: credential proxy and schema-level sensitive-flag that strips payload before persistence
Risk: approval fatigue for frequent low-risk adminlets — mitigation: allow policy to mark adminlets as no-approval-needed after audit history review
Risk: sidecar runner bloat — mitigation: strict size limit and dependency vetting for adminlets
